(a) In General.—Except as provided under subsection (b), the amendments made by this title shall take effect on the later of—
        (1) October 1, 2012; or 
        (2) the date of the enactment of this title.  
    (b) Exception.—Fees under part 8 of subchapter C of chapter VII of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, as added by this title, shall be assessed for all biosimilar biological product applications received on or after October 1, 2012, regardless of the date of the enactment of this title.

fable.w: This section only sets the effective date of the amendments and specifies when biosimilar application fees begin to be assessed. The tempting reading is that the reference to "applications" involves outside parties, but applications are excluded by the definition, and no outside party is consulted or given a right to comment, object, or sue over any federal decision.

It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. The mention of 'applications' refers to the submission of documents for regulatory review, which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.

opus.w: This section only sets when the title's amendments take effect and when fees apply. The mention of product applications might look like outside parties taking part, but applying for approval is not participation under the definition. Nothing here requires consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue.

opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** The words "fees" and "biosimilar biological product applications" might suggest that outside parties are dealing with the FDA. But the definition says applications for licenses or approvals don't count as participation. This section only sets the effective date and says when fees start being charged. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there's no hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely establishes the effective dates for amendments and the timing for fee assessments on biosimilar applications. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in the decision-making process. The mention of 'applications' refers to the submission of documents by companies, which the definition explicitly excludes from participation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section mentions "applications," it involves outside parties (companies) interacting with the government. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" are not participation. Furthermore, this section only sets effective dates and fee assessment rules; it does not describe a process of consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made.
